message.content:
The most recent estimate of the United States’ Gini coefficient—an index of income inequality ranging from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (maximum inequality)—is **about 0.42**.

| Source | Year | Gini Coefficient |
|--------|------|------------------|
| World Bank (World Development Indicators) | 2021 | 0.423 |
| U.S. Census Bureau (Income Inequality Data) | 2022 | 0.421 |

These figures reflect the overall distribution of household income across the U.S. population. The slight decline over the past decade indicates a modest reduction in income inequality, though the U.S. remains one of the more unequal economies among OECD countries.
